headline_marked: [[Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir to be sworn in today]] as Bangladesh's 23rd President
headline: Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir to be sworn in today as Bangladesh's 23rd President
summary: Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir, nominated by BNP, secured a landslide victory in the presidential election, defeating his opponent with 255 votes. The ceremony will take place at Bangabhaban.
details: Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir will be sworn in today as the 23rd President of the People's Republic of Bangladesh. The state oath-taking ceremony is scheduled for Friday, August 21, at 7 PM in the Darbar Hall of Bangabhaban.

The Acting Speaker of the Jatiya Sangsad, Barrister Kaiser Kamal, will administer the oath to the newly elected President. The ceremony will be attended by the outgoing President, Prime Minister, Speaker, Chief Justice, cabinet members, chiefs of the three armed forces, diplomats, and other distinguished national and international personalities.

The presidential election was held on Thursday, August 20, at the Jatiya Sangsad Bhaban. Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir, the BNP-nominated candidate, won by a significant margin with 255 direct votes from Members of Parliament.

His sole opponent, Colonel (retd) Oli Ahmad, Chairman of the 11-party alliance's Liberal Democratic Party (LDP), received 88 votes. Following the vote count, Chief Election Officer and Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) A.M.M. Nasir Uddin officially declared Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir as the victorious presidential candidate.
Subsequently, a government gazette confirming his election was issued, signed by Akhtar Ahmed, Senior Secretary of the Election Commission.
caption:
Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir is set to take the oath as the 23rd President of Bangladesh today. He secured a landslide victory in the recent presidential election.

Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir will be sworn in today as the 23rd President of the People's Republic of Bangladesh. The state oath-taking ceremony is scheduled for Friday, August 21, at 7 PM in the Darbar Hall of Bangabhaban.

The Acting Speaker of the Jatiya Sangsad, Barrister Kaiser Kamal, will administer the oath to the newly elected President. The ceremony will be attended by the outgoing President, Prime Minister, Speaker, Chief Justice, cabinet members, chiefs of the three armed forces, diplomats, and other distinguished national and international personalities.

The presidential election was held on Thursday, August 20, at the Jatiya Sangsad Bhaban. Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir, the BNP-nominated candidate, won by a significant margin with 255 direct votes from Members of Parliament.

His sole opponent, Colonel (retd) Oli Ahmad, Chairman of the 11-party alliance's Liberal Democratic Party (LDP), received 88 votes. Following the vote count, Chief Election Officer and Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) A.M.M. Nasir Uddin officially declared Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir as the victorious presidential candidate.

Subsequently, a government gazette confirming his election was issued, signed by Akhtar Ahmed, Senior Secretary of the Election Commission.

headline: Pakistan's Supreme Court orders Imran Khan to hospital for treatment amid political crisis
summary: The court's directive, including allowing his own doctor and family contact, highlights the unusual state of basic rights in Pakistan, where such provisions are now seen as major constitutional achievements.
details: Former Prime Minister Imran Khan has become a significant political problem for Pakistan's ruling establishment. His continued existence in prison creates discomfort for the current system, while his death in custody could lead to severe accusations against it.

The latest major development saw Pakistan's Supreme Court order the 73-year-old former premier to be transferred to Shifa International Hospital for treatment. The court also directed that his personal physician be included in the medical board and that he be allowed regular contact with family members.

In a normal constitutional system, these would not be considered special privileges but rather standard rights for a prisoner. However, in Pakistan, basic rights have been so restricted for so long that a prisoner's access to medical treatment is now viewed as a major constitutional achievement.

The unusual nature of the situation was further highlighted when the government attempted to appeal a part of the court's ruling. It appears that controlled elections, political interference, widespread lawsuits, political persecution, and the weakening of state institutions are all tolerated, but the question of upholding the constitutional system arises over a former prime minister receiving treatment in a private hospital.

The initial objective of imprisoning Imran Khan was to politically weaken him, keeping him away from public rallies, television, and active politics. The plan involved a continuous barrage of cases against him, exhausting and debilitating his party, and neutralizing him through isolation and state pressure if he proved difficult to defeat in elections.

However, the state's imprisonment of Imran Khan has inadvertently strengthened his political symbolism. While a healthy prisoner can be controlled, a prisoner visibly weakening physically in public view becomes an accusation against the state. Should a prisoner die in custody, they become a part of history.

This dilemma extends to Field Marshal Asim Munir and Pakistan's two dynastic political families (Sharif and Bhutto-Zardari families) operating under military patronage. They cannot indefinitely present themselves as parties deprived of their constitutional rights while simultaneously benefiting from a political system that has sidelined their main rival.

If Imran Khan were to die in prison, the situation would escalate beyond mere political management, potentially transforming into a political explosion. A living politician can be denied, criticized, ridiculed, blamed, or even defeated in elections. However, complexities surrounding a deceased political prisoner tend to fade with time, simplifying and symbolizing their memory.
caption:
